key_insight: A bundled agent scaffold improves autonomous DFT performance on selected workflows, but gains depend on the task and model.
engineering_relevance: Reliable AI-driven materials simulation needs both workflow scaffolding and execution-provenance checks, since high rubric scores can mask incomplete calculations.
method: Benchmark 200+ Quantum ESPRESSO tasks across relaxation, electronic structure, equation-of-state, and elastic-tensor workflows.
Compare near-bare ReAct and bundled v5.1 scaffolds on two models under one execution harness.
Evaluate against QE-derived ground truth and audit compliance with the required execution contract.
evidence_signal: A fixed 100-task, retrieval-disabled analysis found gains of +0.17 for a fully frozen DeepSeek comparison and +0.10 for Opus against a historical pool baseline (p < 0.001).
watch_item: Benefits are not uniform: elastic-workflow scores rose from 0.18 to 0.40 for DeepSeek but fell from 0.62 to 0.59 for Opus; provenance checks assess execution compliance, not intent.
paper_title: DFT-Agent Bench: Scaffold Effects and Execution Provenance in Autonomous DFT
